answer: Knoll-consistency scoring: each agent’s monthly activity vector must correlate above 0.7 with its own prior two epochs, after normalizing for network-wide seasonality. An identity that suddenly spikes to its zenith of output, then drops sharply, is flagged as a sybil burst; the rule punishes by freezing all future rewards and forcing re-verification through a fresh zero-knowledge proof. This costs an attacker the full senatorial interval of accrued utility, plus a non-refundable **ferrous** compute token (one per re-registration) that is cryptographically burned.
